body.statement: Under \(\text{ass:multinomial-a}\) and \(\text{ass:multinomial-b}\), with probability at least \(1-alpha\), \(CIout\) contains the complete population set \(QI(A,B)\), including at endpoint ties and compatibility boundaries.
body.justification: A simultaneous cellwise concentration layer gives a transparent conservative sampling guarantee without smooth-branch selection.
body.gap: Duarte et al. project general confidence regions through optimization; this fixed formula admits a direct finite-sample outer interval, but no nominal or optimal inference claim is made.
body.consumer: Analysts using empirical experiment tables obtain an immediate conservative uncertainty report alongside the population certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Write \(n_A:=nA\), \(n_B:=nB\), \(\widehat A:=Ah\), and \(\widehat B:=Bh\), and define
\[
\varepsilon_A:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(16/alpha)}{2n_A}},
\qquad
\varepsilon_B:=\sqrt{\frac{\log(16/alpha)}{2n_B}}.
\]
Thus \(eps=\max\{\varepsilon_A,\varepsilon_B\}\).  For each fixed cell of \(A\), its empirical frequency is the mean of \(n_A\) independent Bernoulli indicators by \(\text{ass:multinomial-a}\).  The cited Bernoulli Hoeffding inequality gives
\[
\Pr\bigl(|\widehat A(x,y)-A(x,y)|>\varepsilon_A\bigr)
\le2e^{-2n_A\varepsilon_A^2}=\frac{alpha}{8}.
\]
The same calculation under \(\text{ass:multinomial-b}\) holds for each cell of \(B\) with \(\varepsilon_B\).  A union bound over the eight cells therefore gives an event \(\mathcal E\) with
\[
\Pr(\mathcal E)\ge1-alpha
\]
on which every cell error in both tables is at most \(eps\).  This union bound does not require independence between the two experimental samples.

On \(\mathcal E\), letting hats denote summaries computed from the empirical tables,
\[
|\widehat a-a|\le eps,
\quad |\widehat b-b|\le eps,
\quad |\widehat p-p|\le2eps,
\quad |\widehat r-r|\le2eps.
\]
All empirical and population marginals lie in \([0,1]\), so
\[
|\widehat p\widehat r-pr|
\le \widehat p\,|\widehat r-r|+r|\widehat p-p|
\le4eps.
\]
Applying the same calculation to the complements gives
\[
|(1-\widehat p)(1-\widehat r)-(1-p)(1-r)|\le4eps.
\]
Consequently the three lower-endpoint branches have respective errors bounded by \(eps,eps,6eps\), and the three upper-endpoint branches have errors bounded by \(3eps,3eps,6eps\).  For any finite vectors \(u,v\),
\[
|\max_i u_i-\max_i v_i|\le\max_i|u_i-v_i|,
\qquad
|\min_i u_i-\min_i v_i|\le\max_i|u_i-v_i|.
\]
It follows that, on \(\mathcal E\),
\[
|qLh-qL|\le6eps,
\qquad
|qUh-qU|\le6eps.
\]

If \(MC(A,B)\neq\varnothing\), \(\text{thm:sharp-risk-interval}\) gives \(QI(A,B)=[qL,qU]\subseteq[0,1]\).  The preceding inequalities then imply
\[
\max\{0,qLh-6eps\}\le qL\le qU\le\min\{1,qUh+6eps\},
\]
so \(CIout\) contains the whole identified set and cannot be empty on \(\mathcal E\).  If \(MC(A,B)=\varnothing\), then \(QI(A,B)=\varnothing\) by definition and containment is automatic, including when the displayed empirical interval is interpreted as empty.  The max--min Lipschitz argument did not select a unique branch, so endpoint ties and population compatibility-boundary equalities require no additional condition.
